neet_che_u04_t09_1.working: From ΔG° = −RT ln K, a positive ΔG° means ln K < 0. So K < 1 and reactants are favoured.

neet_che_u04_t09_4.working: A: ΔG° < 0 gives K > 1 (III). B: ΔG° = 0 gives K = 1 (I). C: at equilibrium ΔG = 0 and Q = K (IV). D: a tenfold rise in K lowers ΔG° by 2.303RT ≈ 5.7 kJ/mol (II).

neet_che_u04_t09_5.working: A is true: ΔG = 0 at equilibrium, but ΔG° is generally nonzero. B is true: equal concentrations give K = 1, so ΔG° = 0 and ΔS° = ΔH°/T. C is true: ΔG = RT ln(Q/K), which is negative when Q < K. D is false: K = 10⁻³ gives ΔG° = +17.1 kJ/mol, not −17.1.
